decisions.evidence: r2 maker goal summary lists only 'support tags and search, allow a read-later flow, avoid stale clutter and duplicates' — no sorting/filtering. r2 client: 'when I say "organize," I mean more than just tagging. I want to be able to sort and filter my list'.
decisions.note: Specification/direction gate. The asked-about scope omitted list filtering (REF-BM-11) and sorting (REF-BM-22); client requested these reference requirements, so extend. Later implemented conforming at r14-16.

decisions.evidence: r2 maker summary omits saved searches. r2 client: 'eventually save the searches I use often so I can pull them up again quickly.'
decisions.note: Direction gate. Client elicited the saved-view/bundle requirement (REF-BM-29) missing from the summary -> extend. Distinct from the excluded-tags divergence recorded later at r17-19.

decisions.evidence: r2 maker summary has only vague 'avoid stale clutter'. r2 client: 'tucking away things I'm done with so they're out of my everyday list without being deleted for good. Deleting should be its own separate, permanent thing.'
decisions.note: Direction gate. Client specified reversible archive distinct from delete (REF-BM-26/27/28), absent from the asked-about scope -> extend. Implemented conforming at r23-25.

decisions.evidence: r2 client: 'Deleting should be its own separate, permanent thing.' — not present in the r2 maker summary.
decisions.note: Direction gate. Client elicited permanent deletion as a distinct requirement (REF-BM-05) missing from the summary -> extend. Implemented conforming at r26-28.

decisions.evidence: r4 maker presents only the save flow (paste + button -> title/description/source/time/image). r4 client: 'if the app got a detail wrong, I'd like to fix the title or description myself.' r5 maker: 'I'll cover correcting an inaccurate title or description as a separate flow.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. The presented save scope had no editing; client requested the reference edit-details requirement (REF-BM-03) -> extend.

decisions.evidence: r11 maker tag flow is plain typing with no autocomplete ('I assumed tags use short lowercase names and appear...in the sidebar'). r11 client: 'when I start typing a tag I've used before, it should offer it to me so I don't accidentally make a slightly different duplicate.' Delivered r12-13.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Presented tag-entry flow lacked autocomplete; client requested the reference autocomplete requirement (REF-BM-10) -> extend. The r12 type-vs-pick comparison and r13 suggest-mode are the linked disposition of the same decision (counted once).

decisions.evidence: r4 maker: 'each result shows a title, short description, source, saved time, and preview image' — no favicon. Reference REF-BM-02 collects favicon and REF-BM-07 exposes favicon per item. r4 client approves ('The saved item is exactly what I was hoping for') without mentioning favicon.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Presented card substitutes textual 'source' for the reference favicon asset; a difference in fulfilment, not merely equivalent UI. Client approved without surfacing it -> unexpressed. Lower-confidence but establishable from the enumerated fields.

decisions.evidence: r9 maker: 'search should check titles, descriptions, and websites.' r10 gate repeats title/description/website. Reference REF-BM-12 requires full-text over title, description, note, AND url. r9-10 client approves ('that matches my intent') without noting note-search absence.
decisions.note: Prototype/spec gate. Presented search scope omits the note field required by REF-BM-12; established independently from the enumerated fields. Client approved without expressing the difference -> unexpressed. (Advanced operators REF-BM-14/15/16 were never presented, so not classified as decisions.)

decisions.evidence: r8 gate: 'changing the title or description and saving updates the card'; r46-47 gate: 'a non-empty title is required; a description may be empty' — the edit-details flow edits only title/description. Reference REF-BM-04 requires editing url (and note) too. Client approves both gates ('that matches my intent').
decisions.note: Spec gate. Presented edit flow cannot edit the url field required by REF-BM-04 (tags are editable via the separate r11-13 flow; note is extended). Divergence established from the stated editable fields; client never surfaced url editing -> unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: r17/r19 gate: saved view stores 'the current search text, tag filter, and sort order.' Reference REF-BM-29 / Bundle entity = search term + included tags + excluded tags. r17-19 client approves without noting excluded-tags support is absent.
decisions.note: Spec gate, same requirement as the r2 extend but a distinct later decision about completeness. Presented saved view lacks the excluded-tags dimension of the reference bundle (and its single-tag filter has no included/excluded split). Divergence established from the gate text; unexpressed by the client.

decisions.evidence: r29 maker: 'click the title ... Then use Back to bookmarks' opens the saved local copy on a reading page, with a separate 'Try original page' for the live url. Reference REF-BM-08: selecting a list item navigates to the original url. r29 client: 'the saved copy still gives me the full article' — embraces opening the copy, never states an expectation of navigating to the original.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Primary item selection opens the offline saved copy rather than the original url (REF-BM-08); functionally different fulfilment, not equivalent UI. Client approved without expressing the reference expectation -> unexpressed (not accepted_divergence, since no explicit statement of the difference).

decisions.evidence: r4-5 maker: paste one link + one button -> recognizable bookmark with title/description/source/time/preview. r5 client: 'Paste a link, click once, and get back a bookmark I can actually recognize ... exactly the effortless save I wanted.'
decisions.note: Prototype review + spec gate. Core save-by-url behavior conforms to REF-BM-01 (favicon aspect recorded separately).

decisions.evidence: r11-13: adding 'animals' alongside 'science', multiple tags on a bookmark and in the sidebar. r11 client: 'Being able to put more than one tag on a thing and see them listed in the sidebar is just what I wanted.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Assigning one or more tags conforms to REF-BM-09.

decisions.evidence: r14-16: 'animals' tag filter narrows list, 'Oldest first' reorders, filter+sort combine, list starts newest-first. r16 client: 'tag controls that narrow it right away ... reorder by date saved or by title ... filter and sort work together.'
decisions.note: Prototype/spec gate. Tag filtering (REF-BM-11) and sorting (REF-BM-22) implemented conforming (same requirements elicited at r2).

decisions.evidence: r20-22: 'Read later' queues an item, queue shows only pending, 'Mark as read' removes from queue while bookmark stays in All bookmarks. r22 client: 'that's exactly the read-later flow I wanted, and clearly separate from deleting.'
decisions.note: Prototype/spec gate. Read-later lifecycle conforms to REF-BM-17/18/19.

decisions.evidence: r23-25: Archive removes from everyday list without changing details, Archive section keeps it, Restore returns it; clearly separate from permanent deletion. r25 client: 'reversible tuck-away ... clearly distinct from permanent deletion.'
decisions.note: Prototype/spec gate. Archive lifecycle conforms to REF-BM-26/27/28 (requirement elicited at r2).

decisions.evidence: r26-28: 'Delete permanently' in menu, warning naming the bookmark and stating no undo, confirming removes it and all details without moving to Archive. r28 client: 'the deliberate, permanent delete I wanted, clearly separate from the reversible archive.'
decisions.note: Prototype/spec gate. Permanent deletion conforms to REF-BM-05 and the archive/delete distinction REF-BM-27.

decisions.evidence: r32-33: re-saving the same url with extra tracking text is recognized as already saved, no second copy, points to the existing bookmark with details/date intact. r33 client: 'not creating a second bookmark ... pointing me to the original item.'
decisions.note: Prototype/spec gate. Duplicate handling converges to the existing item, conforming to REF-BM-06 (url-normalization is an enhancement, not a divergence).

decisions.evidence: r29-31 and r52: saving captures a readable copy (title/description/source/author-date/image/page text) shown on a focused reading page, labeled with capture date, frozen at save time. r31 client: 'still there and still makes sense even if the page disappears.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Offline page preservation conforms to REF-BM-24's intent of a local snapshot; single-file-HTML fidelity and the PDF special-case rule were never presented (coverage gaps, not classified). REF-BM-25 (Internet Archive) never presented.
